title: The proteomics effects of HSP60 chaperone deficiency in zebrafish larvae
projectDescription: To understand the effects of Hsp60 deficiency in developing vertebrates, we generated CRISPR/Cas9-mediated hspd1 knockout zebrafish lines by targeting exon 2 to induce a frameshift mutation. We selected an allele with a 56 base pair deletion inducing a frameshift mutation leading to loss of protein functions. We examined the proteome changes in zebrafish larvae at 5 days post fertilization (DPF).   Wildtype control and hspd1-/- larvae at 5dpf, were analyzed by TMT and nanoLC-MS/MS based proteomcis. For this purpose, we studied five pools from each genotype, and each pool consisted of five larvae.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Zebrafish animal model larvae pellets were lysed in 1%SDS in 100 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate (TEAB). Zebrafish larvae were additionally homogenized by a motorized pellet pestle (Kimble; #Z359971). All samples were further lysed by sonication with a microtip sonicator (Branson Sonifier 250; Branson Ultrasonics). Protein concentrations were determined with the BCA protein assay (Thermo Scientific; #10678484).  The zebrafish samples were tagged with TMT10plex™ Isobaric Label Reagent Set (Thermo Scientific, #90111). From each sample, 80 µg total protein was in-solution trypsin digested and TMT labeled according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Following the TMT labeling, all samples within each study were pooled. After a strong cation exchange (SCX) purification (Phenomenex, #8B-S010-EAK), peptides were loaded to an Immobiline™ DryStrip Gel (GE Healthcare, #11534985) isoelectric focusing (IEF) separation was performed. The IEF gels were then cut into ten equal pieces, purified in PepClean C18 spin columns (Thermo Scientific, #11824141) according to the manufacturer’s instructions, and then vacuum centrifuged until dryness and stored at -20°C until nanoLC-MS/MS analyses.  Nano-liquid chromatography tandem-mass spectrometry (nanoLC-MS/MS) was performed on an EASY nanoLC-1200 coupled to a Q-Exactive™ HF-X Quadrupole-Orbitrap™ Mass Spectrometer (Thermo Scientific). The analytical column was EASY-Spray PepMap RSLC C18, 2µm, 100 Å, 75 µM x 25 cm (Thermo Scientific). A 170-minute gradient in 5-40 % acetonitrile, 0.1 % formic acid was applied. The normalized collision energy (NCE) of 35% was applied for higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) for the peptide fragmentation. Full scan (MS1) and fragment scan resolutions were set at 60,000 and 45,000, respectively. Automatic gain control (AGC) for MS1 and MS2 were set at 1x106 with a scan range between 392-1,500 m/z and at 1x105 with a fixed mass of 110 m/z, respectively. Up to 12 of the most intense peaks of the full scan were fragmented with data-dependent analysis (DDA). Unassigned and +1 charge states were excluded from fragmentation, and the dynamic exclusion duration was 15 seconds. Each fraction was LC-MS/MS analyzed twice, where peptides identified from >9 scans in the first analysis were excluded from fragmentation in the second analysis.
dataProcessingProtocol: All LC-MS/MS results were merged and submitted for the database search for identification and quantification of proteins using Proteome Discoverer 3.0 (Thermo Scientific). The reference proteome for zebrafish (UP000000437; downloaded on 02.12.2022) contained 46,691 Danio rerio Uniprot sequences. The following TMT labels were used for the 5 wild type samples 126, 127N, 127C, 128N and 128C, whereas 129N 129C, 130N, 130C and 131 were used for the knock-out samples. Precursor mass tolerance was 10 ppm, and fragment mass tolerance was 20 mmu. Maximum number  missed cleavages was 2. Oxidation of methionine was set as dynamic modification and static modifications were carbamidomethylation of cysteines and TMT-plex-labels on lysine and peptide N-terminus. The co-isolation threshold was set at 35%, and the identification false discovery rate was 0.01 at both peptide and protein levels. Proteins with at least 3 quantitative peptide scans and at least one unique peptide were considered as quantified and included in the further proteomics data analysis. Criteria for the differentially expressed proteins were set at p<0.05 and |FC|>1.2 for protein abundance.
